messages:
anya: quick heads-up — beryl (embed-3-small) int8 run shows a reproducible recall@10 drop on our multilingual holdout. not huge but consistent: ~0.86 -> 0.78 on the wiki-multi set.

mike: ugh. is that after L2-normalizing embeddings?

anya: yes. ran normalize -> build index -> recall. same workflow as fp16.

julia: did you compare cosine distances pre/post quant? maybe angular distortion.

anya: good call. I computed pairwise cosine diffs on a 2k sample: mean delta ~0.04, but the tail (99th pct) hits 0.22. clustering visuals look smeared.

sanjay: can you paste the recall calc? quick check of metric impl.

anya: sure — code I used:

```
# compute recall@k
embs_fp = load_embeddings('fp16.npy')
embs_q = load_embeddings('int8.npy')
idx = faiss.IndexFlatIP(dim)
faiss.normalize_L2(embs_fp)
faiss.normalize_L2(embs_q)
idx.add(embs_fp)
D, I = idx.search(embs_q, k=10)
recall = compute_recall(I, ground_truth_ids)
print(recall)
```

mike: looks fine. are you quantizing in 1-pass per-channel or symmetric per-tensor?

anya: current pipeline uses per-tensor static quantization via ONNX QAT export -> dynamic quantize. maybe that's the issue.

marco: try per-channel int8 on the final projection (the 2-layer dense) only? sometimes projection weights are most sensitive and cause direction shifts.

anya: will try. also saw PCA variance explained drop: top-10 components explain 46% FP16 -> 32% INT8. weird.

julia: that suggests anisotropy / dimensional collapse changes. plotting centroids before/after would help.

eval-bot: automated sanity checks finished — pairwise cosine correlation between fp16/int8 = 0.92, norm distribution mean(fp16)=1.0002 mean(int8)=0.9987, nearest-neighbor overlap@10=0.80 (detailed CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-ml/beryl/quant-audit/2012468101/).

mike: overlap@10 0.80 aligns with recall drop. can you run ef/search sweeps? maybe HNSW params mask quality loss.

anya: ran ef_search 128 -> 512; recall improves about +0.02 at ef=512 but still below fp16 baseline.

sanjay: next checks: 1) per-channel quant for projection layer, 2) asymmetric quant (zero-point) option, 3) try post-quant bias correction (PTQ bias correction), 4) float16 mixed precision where only KV/cache stays int8?

anya: noted. I'll run per-channel and bias-corrected PTQ today. also testing cosine vs L2 indexing — recall shift slightly different by metric.

julia: add diagnostics: for a 200-sample failure subset, show nearest neighbors indices pre/post and nearest distance delta. helps spot consistent swaps vs random noise.

anya: doing that now. early signal: many failures are cross-lingual pairs where tokens are sparse — maybe embedding magnitude change matters.

marco: also check tokenizer seed/ordering; tiny tokenization changes sometimes amplify on multilingual sets.

anya: good point, will freeze tokenizer and rerun. will post short summary + plots here when done. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — LMK if you want help running per-channel export or cluster for large runs.
